context.decision_0003_divergence_sign_off: AGREE. REVIEWER's sign-off recorded 2026-08-30 in lib/letflow/design/req191-service-catalog-core.md section 0 (full reasoning block), mirrored in lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex's moduledoc and the migration's header comment. The global-table divergence is structurally justified independent of the solution_pack_installs precedent it cites (that analogy is imperfect -- solution_pack_installs is global for operational-infrastructure reasons, not because a single row must be visible from every tenant's schema simultaneously); service_catalog's own argument is sufficient on its own: a scope=:global row must be visible identically from every tenant at once (schema-per-tenant cannot express this without replication-plus-sync machinery Decision B doesn't provide), and service_id must be globally unique across all tenants and both scopes (a per-schema unique index cannot enforce this at all). Consequence noted for TEST-DESIGNER: get_for_tenant/2's visibility predicate is now the SOLE tenant-isolation mechanism for this data (no physical schema separation backstopping it) -- this makes the three-way visibility acceptance criterion especially load-bearing; do not treat it as an ordinary business-rule test.

type_safety_finding_for_orch_to_file.title: Letflow.ServiceCatalog's scope-typed attrs accept atom() | String.t() instead of the narrower :global | :tenant, even though Ecto.Enum already constrains the column
type_safety_finding_for_orch_to_file.description: register_attrs.scope and update_scope_attrs.scope in lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex type as atom() | String.t() rather than :global | :tenant, though the Entry schema's Ecto.Enum field already constrains the DB column to exactly those two values. A caller passing an arbitrary string only fails at Repo.insert/Repo.update time via the changeset, not at compile/dialyzer time -- a class of invalid input a tighter @type could make unrepresentable at the type-check layer instead of relying solely on the runtime changeset/DB constraint. Non-blocking (does not affect REVIEWER's PASS) but worth tracking as the schema grows.

acceptance_criteria: the service_catalog table carries the scope/owner consistency CHECK: an insert with scope 'global' and a non-null owner_tenant_id is rejected by the DATABASE, and so is one with scope 'tenant' and a null owner_tenant_id -- two explicit tests, not changeset-level validation
required_auth and timeout_ms are CHECK constrained at the database level: an insert with required_auth 'BASIC' is rejected, and so is one with timeout_ms 0 and one with timeout_ms 3600001

get_for_tenant/2 returns a global service to any tenant; returns a tenant-scoped service to its owner; and returns NOT FOUND -- not a forbidden error -- for a tenant-scoped service owned by a different tenant, so the two cases are indistinguishable to the caller (three explicit tests)
service_id is globally unique: registering the same service_id for a second, different tenant fails, even when the first is tenant-scoped
register/1 with scope 'tenant' naming a tenant that does not exist is rejected without creating a row

delete/1 of a service referenced by an ACTIVE definition is refused and the error names the referencing definition ids; delete/1 of an unreferenced service succeeds -- and a test confirms the reference check matches an actual SERVICE_TASK service_id attribute rather than a substring of the serialized graph, by registering a service whose id appears only inside an unrelated string in some definition's graph and asserting that definition does NOT block the delete

update_scope/2 narrowing a global service to tenant-scoped is refused, naming the conflicting tenant ids, when another tenant's ACTIVE definition references it; widening a tenant-scoped service to global is always allowed

Letflow.Definitions.ServiceScopeValidator.validate/3 works unchanged when handed a Lookup backed by this catalog (scope_validator_lookup/1): a definition referencing a service not visible to its tenant is rejected at activation, and one referencing a visible service activates -- with no change to service_scope_validator.ex itself, confirmed by git diff
